description: When does the snail reach the top?
statement: 10 m pole, +3 m by day, -2 m by night
statement_latex: \begin{gathered}10\text{ m pole}\\+3\text{ by day}\\-2\text{ by night}\end{gathered}
solution_sketch: The net gain over a full day-night is 1 m, which suggests 10 days - the trap. But on the day the snail's daytime climb first reaches the top it never slips back. After night 7 it is at 7 m; on day 8 it climbs 7 + 3 = 10 and is out. Answer: day 8.
difficulty_rationale: Naive route: net progress is 3 - 2 = 1 m per day, so 10 m looks like 10 days. That is the wrong answer and the whole point of the puzzle. Insight: the slip only happens if the snail is still on the pole at nightfall, so the last day's 3 m climb is not reduced - you must track the height at the end of each night and find the first day whose daytime climb crosses 10. After the insight there are two cheap steps: after night k the height is k metres, and you need k + 3 >= 10, giving k = 7 and so day 8. Seeing that the final day breaks the 1-m-per-day pattern, rather than dividing 10 by 1, takes real thought yet no paper - comfortably a 40-second puzzle and a classic 20-second trap.
